official.deadline_note: There are no deadlines - applications can be made at any time of year. Only one funding application in any 12-month period; rejected applicants must wait 12 months before reapplying; funded applicants cannot apply again for at least 12 months.
official.application_cycle: Rolling - no fixed intake or cycle; applications accepted at any time of year
official.status_note: Rolling programme with no published closing date; the Foundation site and application portal remained active through 2026 (latest news item 28 Aug 2026, and a joint applicant-guidance webinar series launched 30 Jan 2026).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Only fieldwork/project costs are considered - the Foundation states 'we cannot cover academic fees', so tuition is not funded.
official.funding_period: one-off grant; follow-on stages up to £8k/£12k/£18k
benefits: Staged four-stage funding process: 1st Rufford Small Grant up to £7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to £8,000, Booster Grant up to £12,000, Completion Grant up to £18,000

Funds are paid to an organisation of the applicant's choice (e.g. a nature conservation NGO or university) that agrees to receive and manage them; the applicant need not work for that organisation and it may be based in another country
Every grantee receives a webpage hosting project updates and the final report
Applications accepted at any time of year - there are no deadlines
Access to Rufford learning events that build grantee capacity and networks
eligibility: Applicants should be in the early stages of their conservation careers - priority is funding those undertaking an MSc or PhD (or equivalent) or who graduated from such studies in the past 3 years; BSc students are not funded and career-changers to conservation later in life are considered

Projects must have a nature conservation focus, be small-scale or pilot projects, take place in an eligible country (around 150 developing and emerging economy countries), and claim only fieldwork costs - the Foundation cannot cover academic fees
Ideally the Foundation should provide between 50 and 100% of the costs of the project; where it is not the only funder, evidence of co-funding is required
Species-focused projects must concern species not listed as Least Concern at a global level on the IUCN Red List (unassessed species thought to be globally threatened are also considered)
Exclusions: pure research with no obvious conservation benefit, expeditions (particularly where the applicant must raise funds to participate), attending conferences or seminars, and publishing books
requirements: The application and the references must be submitted in English
Only one funding application in any 12-month period per applicant
The project must not already have begun at the time of application
An organisation (e.g. conservation NGO or university) must be arranged before applying to receive and manage the funds
Three references must be provided; applications cannot be processed until they are received
Applications are only accepted online via the Rufford application portal; an account must be created before first submission
documents: Completed online application form via the Rufford application portal (account required; form questions also downloadable in Word for offline preparation)
Three references submitted confidentially and directly by the referees to The Rufford Foundation
Evidence of co-funding from other sources where The Rufford Foundation is not the only funder (required at Booster and Completion stages)
Regular project updates posted on the grantee's Rufford webpage during the project
Final evaluation report submitted using the Foundation's final report template on project completion
selection_criteria: Two-stage review: the Foundation office first screens all applications against its basic criteria (rejection possible within days of submission), then applications that pass go to external expert review
Applications that pass to external review receive a decision within 4 months of submission

Published decision inputs: early-career status, nature conservation focus, eligible country, threatened species/habitat status (IUCN rule), small-scale/pilot nature, and - for follow-up stages - completion of the previous project with updates and final report
Completion stage applications are expected to show a sustainability plan and co-funding matching the amount requested
coverage: Subsistence, travel and accommodation costs incurred in delivering the project (field and living costs)
Essential payments to individuals assisting the project, e.g. drivers, porters or guides
Organisation management fee/overheads of up to 10% of the overall value of the grant may be accepted
Not covered: academic fees, salaries (generally), publication costs (generally), international travel costs (generally)
application_method: Check the general criteria, FAQs and eligible-country list, and prepare answers using the published form-questions document
Create a user account on the Rufford application portal with a valid email address
Complete and submit the online application form (strict word limits; submitted applications are final and cannot be edited)
Arrange for an organisation (conservation NGO or university) to receive and manage the funds
Nominate three referees who submit their references directly; the application is not processed until all three have arrived
Track application progress online until decision
official.application_route: Online only via apply.ruffordsmallgrants.org - create an account, complete the English application form online, and secure three references submitted directly by referees to the Foundation.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants may be based in an advanced economy, but the project itself must be in an eligible country; projects in the UK, US and other advanced economies do not qualify, and some countries (e.g. Afghanistan, Belarus, Cuba, Iran, Myanmar, North Korea, Russia, Sudan, Syria, Venezuela, West Bank and Gaza) are currently unable to be considered, with Ukraine partial (excluding Crimea, Donetsk, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia and Luhansk).
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants of any nationality based in any country, provided the project takes place in an eligible (developing or emerging economy) country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Projects must have a nature conservation focus: particular species (not globally Least Concern on the IUCN Red List), threatened habitats, or issues such as human-wildlife conflict or community education.
official.description: The Rufford Foundation is a UK registered charity that funds nature conservation projects across the developing world. Its flagship Rufford Small Grants Programme gives funding to individuals working in developing countries who are starting on the ladder of conservation research and establishing pilot programmes, and since it began it has awarded in excess of £30 million through more than 5,100 grants to projects in over 150 countries.
official.region: Global - developing and emerging economy countries on the eligible-country list
official.program_type: Staged nature conservation fieldwork project grants (1st RSG, 2nd RSG, Booster Grant, Completion Grant)
official.english_requirement: The application and the three references must be submitted in English (no language test score is published).

typical award size (only maximum amounts per stage are published)
verification.notes: Amounts (£7,000/£8,000/£12,000/£18,000), rolling deadlines, English-language rule, fieldwork-only coverage, reference rules and duration all read live from the official Rufford application portal help pages and rufford.org news/about pages on 2026-10-10.

applicant_utility.summary: Rufford money buys fieldwork, not a degree: it pays for conservation work on the ground in roughly 150 developing and emerging countries, with caps rising from £7,000 to £18,000 as you progress through four stages. Because funds are paid to an NGO or university rather than to you, the most common blocker is having no organisation ready to accept and manage the grant before you apply. The programme never closes, so your real enemies are the 12-month reapply lockout after a rejection and the 12-week reference deadline - if all three references have not arrived by then, the application is rejected and you wait a year to try again.
applicant_utility.best_fit: MSc/PhD conservationists (or within 3 years of graduating) in an eligible country who need their first £7,000 of field budget for threatened species or habitat work.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a named organisation (NGO or university) that agrees to receive and manage the grant before you open the form - money is never paid to personal accounts, and an overhead request above 10% forces you to find another organisation.

Line up three referees with the exact required mix: one from a well-established institution (major conservation NGO, university or government body), one based in your project country, one from outside it; if you are an MSc/PhD student one must be your supervisor, and no two referees from the same institution.
Brief referees so they can write independently - references go straight to Rufford and are confidential; drafting or ghost-writing your own reference gets the application rejected.
Draft answers offline from the published form-questions document and respect the strict word limits, because anything over the limit cannot be pasted into the online form.

Build the budget from fieldwork items only - subsistence, local travel and accommodation, field assistants such as drivers/porters/guides - and leave out tuition, your salary, publication charges and international flights.
Confirm before investing effort that your project country is on the eligible list and any target species is not globally Least Concern on the IUCN Red List.
common_rejection_risks: Missing references: the application is not processed without three, and if they have not all arrived 12 weeks after submission it is rejected and you cannot reapply for at least 12 months.
Applying for a project that has already started - Rufford will not fund work already begun, and review can take up to 4 months.
No organisation in place to receive and manage the funds, or a host organisation charging more than a 10% management fee.
A target species listed as globally Least Concern on the IUCN Red List, or a project located in an ineligible (advanced-economy or currently sanctioned) country.
Framing the work as pure research with no obvious conservation benefit, or including conferences, participation expeditions or publishing costs.
Assuming a submitted application can be edited - it is final once submitted, and unsubmitted applications are deleted after 3 months.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and academic fees (explicitly not funded), your own salary (salaries generally not funded), publication charges, international travel to the project country, and any organisational overhead above 10%; at the Booster and Completion stages you must also raise matching co-funding from other donors yourself.
document_audit: The three references are confidential documents sent by referees directly to Rufford - you may only give background project information, never text for a referee to sign.

Referee composition must include an established institution, someone in your project country and someone outside it; MSc/PhD applicants must include their supervisor and cannot use two referees from the same institution.
Co-funding evidence is required whenever Rufford is not the sole funder, and at Completion Grant stage the Foundation expects matching funds from other sources.
The final evaluation report must use the Foundation's template; without it you cannot apply for further funding.
The application form imposes strict word limits and cannot be edited after final submission, so prepare offline using the published Word question list.
alerts: There is no deadline, but only one application is allowed in any 12 months - a rejection locks you out for 12 months, and being funded locks you out for at least 12 months before the next stage.
Applications reaching external review can take up to 4 months to decide, so do not begin the project or commit dates before a decision arrives.
Chase your three referees immediately after submitting: the 12-week reference rule rejects the whole application if they lag.
Keep gaps between Rufford applications under 5 years; longer gaps count against follow-up applications.

Money is paid only to an organisation (NGO or university), never to you personally, and that organisation may be based outside your project country but must have any permissions needed to receive foreign funds.
Any material change to project design or budget after the award must be agreed with the Foundation first, or the full grant may have to be returned.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account at apply.ruffordsmallgrants.org, submit the finalised English form online (no edits afterwards), then track progress while three referee-submitted references arrive - office screening can reject within days, and external-reviewed applications get a decision within 4 months.
